newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-"WE BLEW IT" SAYS SCOTLAND CAPTAIN.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-"WE BLEW IT" SAYS SCOTLAND CAPTAIN.

text.p: Scotland captain Rob Wainwright acknowledged a lack of concentration "cost us the game" against Wales in the opening round of the Five Nations championship.
"We've got to blame ourselves," said Wainwright, reflecting on the three tries between the 51st and 56th minutes which wiped out his side's 16-10 lead and set up Wales's 34-19 win.
"They were real punches in the eye. Letting yourself down in that manner is unforgivable, whether you're being paid for it or not."
Scottish manager Arthur Hastie called it a "fatal five minutes" but the Scottish management all acknowledged the Welsh had taken their chances well.
The impact of former rugby league men Scott Gibbs and Scott Quinnell was immense and Welsh skipper Jonathan Humphreys believes they have transformed his side's prospects.
"They bring a great deal of confidence to the side and they bring a very mature attitude which rubs off on the rest of the players. It takes a big weight off my shoulders," he said.
"It's a great result but now we've got to lay to rest another bogey at home to Ireland in two weeks time." Wales have not beaten Ireland at home since 1983.
Coach Kevin Bowring described it as "one of the most pleasing wins of my career."
"We're heading in the right direction, but there's still a long way to go," he said.
